lead: >-
  In Costa Rica, you can combine scuba diving with tropical rainforests and a journey across the country. On the 5-day Costa Rica Gems tour, diving takes place near Caño Island, while the 13-day Extreme Costa Rica adventure features the Catalina Islands. These are two different parts of the Pacific Ocean and two distinct itineraries. Compare them by diving difficulty, time spent at sea and the route before and after the diving day.
---

## Diving tours in Costa Rica: Caño Island or the Catalina Islands?

**On Ada Tours' current Costa Rica itineraries, diving occupies a separate day, while the rest of the trip focuses on nature, outdoor activities and travel between destinations.** Our collection offers {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring diving and Costa Rica on the route. They differ in overall duration, departure points for sea excursions and the experience expected of divers.

[Costa Rica: True Gems](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-gems/) heads to [Caño Island](/costa-rica/place/cano-island/) off the southern Pacific coast. [Extreme Costa Rica](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/) includes an excursion to the [Catalina Islands](/costa-rica/place/catalina-islands/) in the country's northwest. Both tours offer **one scheduled diving day**, even though the second trip is almost three times as long as the first. The number of individual dives on those days must be confirmed against the particular marine operator's terms.

| Itinerary | Main difference |
|---|---|
| [True Gems, 5 days](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-gems/) | Caño, day 4; Corcovado rainforest |
| [Extreme Costa Rica, 13 days](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/) | Catalina, day 11; demanding active itinerary |

For a broader introduction to the destination, see our [Costa Rica travel guide](/costa-rica/). Here we focus on the actual diving days in these two programs and the details to check before booking. Other parts of Latin America and dedicated underwater experiences appear in the [diving section](/interests/diving/).

## Caño Island: a marine reserve and Corcovado in 5 days

The [5-day True Gems tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-gems/) begins in [San José](/costa-rica/place/san-jose/). On day 2, the itinerary includes a domestic flight to Palmar Sur and a boat journey along the Sierpe River toward the southern [Osa Peninsula](/costa-rica/place/osa-peninsula/). Day 3 is dedicated to [Corcovado National Park](/costa-rica/place/corcovado-national-park/) and walks in the Sirena Station area. **Day 4 is set aside for diving near [Caño Island](/costa-rica/place/cano-island/)**, followed by the return flight on day 5.

This order suits travelers who are equally interested in the underwater world and wildlife in the tropical rainforest. The main emphasis is on [Corcovado](/costa-rica/place/corcovado-national-park/), the coast around [Drake Bay](/costa-rica/place/drake-bay/) and one day at sea. The published itinerary does not advertise an extended series of dives or a separate scuba training course.

The waters around Caño are known for reef areas and a rich variety of marine life. You may encounter turtles, rays, reef fish and other Pacific species. Sightings of particular animals depend on sea conditions; references to manta rays and sharks in the itinerary are not guarantees of encounters.

### Access rules for the Caño marine reserve

[Caño Island](/costa-rica/place/cano-island/) lies within a protected marine area. Under the rules of Costa Rica's National System of Conservation Areas, SINAC, recreational diving and snorkeling are permitted only in designated zones. Visits require advance arrangements and the supervision of a registered professional. Some areas also limit the number of people allowed in the water.

Before traveling, confirm the **entry permit, specific dive site, guiding arrangements, number of boat outings and equipment provided**. The tour's general inclusion terms do not itemize every service supplied by the dive center. Boat trips to this area depart from [Drake Bay](/costa-rica/place/drake-bay/) and the Sierpe area, but their actual schedules depend on the operator and weather.

## The Catalina Islands: diving after rafting and volcanoes

The [13-day Extreme Costa Rica tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/) is designed as a substantial active adventure. It starts with the canals of [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/), then continues with two days of rafting on the [Pacuare River](/costa-rica/place/pacuare-river/), activities around [Arenal and La Fortuna](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) and a visit to [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/). The itinerary then reaches the Pacific coast.

Day 9 offers time to relax by the sea, while day 10 is devoted to sport fishing near [Flamingo](/costa-rica/place/flamingo/). **Day 11 is dedicated to diving near the [Catalina Islands](/costa-rica/place/catalina-islands/)**, day 12 is free, and day 13 brings the airport transfer. The itinerary does not involve daily diving throughout the trip.

Catalina is a group of rocky islands and underwater formations off the Pacific coast of Guanacaste. Boat trips depart from coastal communities, including the Flamingo area. Large rays, reef fish and other marine species attract divers here, although visibility, currents and animal sightings vary even within a single season.

### Who is the Catalina diving day suitable for?

**The diving day in Extreme Costa Rica is described as an activity for experienced participants.** The published itinerary mentions the possibility of strong currents and challenging surface conditions, with a depth range of 12 to 35 m across different sites. Skills in controlled descent, buoyancy and safety stops have practical importance here.

This describes **the particular tour and its intended dives**, not a claim that the entire island group is restricted to advanced divers. Local centers select sites of different difficulty levels. However, the advertised experience cannot simply be replaced with an introductory beginner's dive without prior agreement. Those without diving experience should first discuss another site, training and separate terms.

On the free day by the coast, travelers can stay around [Tamarindo](/costa-rica/place/playa-tamarindo/); no mandatory excursions are scheduled. If you want to spend more time underwater, arrange additional diving days **before** finalizing the itinerary.

## Caño versus Catalina: what should guide your choice?

Both areas are in the Pacific, but they are accessed from different parts of Costa Rica. **Caño** is associated with the southern [Osa Peninsula](/costa-rica/place/osa-peninsula/), boat travel and an itinerary through Corcovado. **Catalina** is off the northwestern coast and combines more naturally with a stay in Guanacaste.

If you want a short nature trip with a scuba day, the [5-day itinerary through Corcovado and Caño](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-gems/) is a logical fit. If you want rafting, canyoning, volcanoes, mountain forests and diving in one journey, the [13-day active tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/) is the stronger choice.

A single calendar day allocated to diving does not necessarily mean the same physical demands. Depth, current, waves, distance to the site and each participant's experience all matter. Beginners should prioritize appropriate conditions and an instructor over choosing an island by its list of marine animals.

To compare the other activities on these routes, explore [Costa Rica adventure tours](/interests/adventure/tours/costa-rica/) and [nature trips in the country](/interests/wildlife/tours/costa-rica/). These are separate collections: not every listed tour includes scuba diving.

## When to travel for diving

Costa Rica's Pacific coast has distinct dry and rainy periods. According to the national tourism authority's climate information, **December–March is usually drier**, April is transitional, rain is more common from May through October, and November is transitional again. This is only a starting point for choosing dive dates: underwater visibility and temperature depend on currents and the specific location.

Around Catalina, dive operators report seasonal changes in marine life and water temperature. Larger rays are more frequently seen in certain months; in others the water is warmer and visibility improves at some sites. The generalization that the dry season always provides the best diving is misleading. Before purchasing a trip, it is more useful to ask which sites operate on your dates and what conditions to expect.

At Caño, sea state, rainfall and the rules of the nature reserve also matter. **No season guarantees that a boat can depart**, that the water will be clear or that a manta ray will appear. If diving is the main reason for traveling, allow some flexibility for changes rather than scheduling your only possible dive immediately before departure.

## Preparation, equipment and flying after diving

Before confirming a tour, discuss the participants' qualifications, permitted depth, number of dives, equipment hire, professional supervision and medical restrictions with the organizer and dive center. Find out separately what happens if a boat trip is canceled because of weather. Our itineraries confirm diving days and general included services, but **they do not establish a universal diving-equipment package or identical eligibility rules** for the two routes.

Return flights deserve particular attention. According to Divers Alert Network (DAN), the minimum interval before flying after one no-decompression dive is **12 hours**; after multiple dives in a day or diving over several days, it is **18 hours**. A longer interval reduces risk, and dives requiring mandatory decompression stops call for substantially more time. These guidelines do not replace an individualized assessment of the actual dive profile or the instructions of a dive computer.

On the [Caño itinerary](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-gems/), dives are scheduled for day 4 and a flight for day 5. **Compare the actual dive and flight times before booking**: the order of days alone does not establish a safe interval. On [Extreme Costa Rica](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/), day 12 is free after the diving scheduled for day 11, with the flight on day 13; the actual times still need to be coordinated.

## Frequently asked questions about diving tours in Costa Rica

### How many diving days are included in each tour?

Under the current itineraries, **each has one diving day**: [Caño](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-gems/) on day 4 of 5, and [Catalina](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/) on day 11 of 13. The number of individual dives is set by the dive center's confirmed timetable.

### Can I join without a diving certification?

That depends on the chosen itinerary and the operator's rules. The [Catalina tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/) explicitly targets experienced participants for its diving day, so it would be wrong to promise that a beginner can take part in the same dives. Introductory activities or other marine options must be discussed separately rather than assumed to be included.

### How is diving at Caño different from snorkeling?

Snorkelers observe marine life from the surface. Scuba diving requires different equipment, preparation and adherence to a dive profile. Both activities are permitted in designated conservation zones around [Caño](/costa-rica/place/cano-island/), but they are not the same service.

### When should I book a dive trip to Caño Island?

Access to the marine reserve is regulated by SINAC and requires advance arrangements. Coordinate permits and the operator when planning the itinerary so the chosen diving day complies with the rules and the site's actual availability.

### Can diving be the main activity throughout the vacation?

On these two itineraries, one underwater day complements a wider nature trip. For several consecutive scuba days, the number of boat outings, accommodation locations and intervals before flights would need to be reviewed separately. Compare other destinations in the [full diving tours catalog](/interests/diving/tours/).

lead: >-
  Diving in Ecuador is primarily associated with the Galápagos Islands: volcanic underwater landscapes, ocean currents, sea turtles, rays, sea lions and sharks. Our dedicated itinerary is based at Hotel Fiesta on Santa Cruz. Both 4-day and 5-day options are available, with 2 dives on each diving day. An up-to-date certification, diving experience and enough time before the return flight are essential considerations when choosing your trip.
---

## Diving in the Galápagos: which Ecuador tour should you choose?

**Ada Tours' main current diving itinerary in Ecuador offers [4 or 5 days in the Galápagos with accommodation at Hotel Fiesta](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-diving-4-5-days/).** This is a trip with organized dive-boat outings, not introductory snorkeling as part of a standard sightseeing cruise. The options differ in the number of diving days and total time spent on the islands.

Our themed catalog includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The geography centers on the [Galápagos archipelago](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/), reached by a separate flight from mainland Ecuador. The base is [Santa Cruz Island](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/), with arrivals and departures through the airport on [Baltra Island](/ecuador/place/baltra-island/).

| Option | Diving |
|---|---|
| 4 days / 3 nights | 2 days, 4 dives |
| 5 days / 4 nights | 3 days, 6 dives |

Each diving day includes **2 dives**, with a surface interval of approximately 1.5 hours. Specific sites, the sequence of visits and whether boats can depart depend on ocean conditions, the dive center's schedule and participants' experience. It would therefore be incorrect to promise Gordon Rocks or another site as a guaranteed stop every day.

## How the Santa Cruz itinerary works

The first day begins on [Baltra](/ecuador/place/baltra-island/). On the way to Hotel Fiesta, guests visit the highlands of [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/), home to giant land tortoises. A separate [guided excursion with lunch](/ecuador/santa-cruz-highlands/santa-cruz-highlands-tortoises-lunch/) is included for this part of the day. After check-in, travelers meet the dive center team and select or check their equipment.

The days at sea follow. The [Galápagos tour](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-diving-4-5-days/) describes a departure around 08:00, a check dive at the start of the diving program, a second descent after the surface interval and a return in the afternoon. Each such day includes a snack and lunch. Return time depends on the dive site selected; the itinerary gives approximate times of 15:15 and 16:30.

The separate excursion product [Galápagos: Diving Day with 2 Dives](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/galapagos-two-dive-day/) illustrates how a day at sea works. However, the existence of this excursion does not mean guests may independently choose any dive location: authorized areas and the actual route are determined by the operator under national park rules.

The 4-day option includes 2 diving days. The 5-day option adds a third outing at sea. The final day of both options consists of breakfast and a transfer to the airport, and the departure flight must be coordinated with the time of the last dive.

## Interesting dive sites around the Galápagos Islands

The underwater scenery of the [Galápagos](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) differs from that of calm tropical lagoons. Volcanic rocks, walls, deeper areas and currents shape the diving. Marine life can include rays, turtles, sea lions and different shark species. No one can guarantee an encounter with a particular animal on an individual outing.

[Gordon Rocks](/ecuador/place/gordon-rocks/) is known for strong currents and opportunities to see hammerhead sharks. It is unsuitable for many levels of experience: access depends on the dive center's assessment and current conditions. Even experienced divers should follow the guide's decision rather than the reputation of a site in promotional descriptions.

[Cousins Rock](/ecuador/place/cousins-rock/) features an underwater wall, reef sections and black coral. The area around [Floreana](/ecuador/place/floreana-island/), with its island coves and volcanic formations, offers a different experience. Possible sites on the tour also include areas near the northern islands and small rocky islets. Treat these as options from which the dive operator builds an itinerary that can actually be run.

The Galápagos National Park authority officially distinguishes marine visitor sites by permitted activities, including scuba diving and snorkeling. Check the authorization to dive and the conditions of a particular site with the operating provider. Choosing a site purely by calendar without considering currents and permits is unreliable.

## Certification, experience and admission requirements

**The advertised certified-diver program requires a PADI, NAUI, CMAS or equivalent qualification.** The stated minimum age is 12. Participants complete a questionnaire before diving; a medical certificate may be required in certain medical circumstances and, where specified by the itinerary, for participants over 60. Read these terms before choosing between 4 and 5 days.

The [diving tour](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-diving-4-5-days/) includes an English-speaking divemaster or naturalist guide and the basic equipment listed in the itinerary: a 5–7 mm wetsuit, regulator, buoyancy compensator, mask, fins, weight system and cylinders. A dive computer, nitrox and certain adapters are listed separately as paid extras. Personal equipment can be checked at the dive center on arrival.

For beginners without certification, separate Discover Scuba Diving experiences and PADI training are available, **but these are separate services with their own conditions**, not an automatic part of the standard tour. Snorkeling, a boat excursion and a scuba dive are distinct activities with different participation requirements. Do not purchase a certified-diver package expecting to replace its diving days with lessons without separate agreement.

### How is Galápagos diving different from snorkeling?

When snorkeling, you observe marine life from the surface using a mask and snorkel. Scuba diving allows you to explore underwater features at depth, but requires buoyancy skills, equipment handling and monitoring of the breathing-gas supply. In the Galápagos, currents, colder water masses and the need to follow the guide's instructions add further considerations.

If you mainly want to discover the islands' nature without diving certification, compare [regular Ecuador tours](/ecuador/tour/) or [cruises and expeditions in Ecuador](/interests/cruises-and-expeditions/tours/ecuador/). Their boat outings and snorkeling should not automatically be treated as equivalent to organized scuba diving.

## What is included, and what costs extra?

Both options list accommodation at Fiesta, breakfasts and lunches according to the schedule, designated group transfers and excursions, boat outings with 2 dives on diving days and the listed basic equipment. Breakfast is included on departure day.

**Charged separately:** flights between mainland Ecuador and the Galápagos, national park entrance fees, the Transit Control Card, insurance, tips and some equipment options. The [specific tour conditions](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-diving-4-5-days/) show prices for both 4 and 5 days, including the difference between double and single occupancy. Compare those prices only for the same room category.

Sea conditions and decisions by the protected area's administration can alter the selection of dive sites. This also applies to the option with three diving days booked in advance. When arranging the trip, it is particularly helpful to disclose your certification level, the date of your most recent dive and any relevant medical restrictions early.

## Flying after diving: why enough time matters

After several dives, the body needs time before ascending to altitude. This includes flying from [Baltra](/ecuador/place/baltra-island/) back to mainland Ecuador. Divers Alert Network recommends **at least 18 hours at the surface before flying** after multiple no-decompression dives in one day or diving on several days. A longer interval reduces risk, and the actual requirement may be stricter depending on the dive profile or individual circumstances.

On the [Hotel Fiesta itinerary](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-diving-4-5-days/), travelers are advised to coordinate the timing of the final day at sea and the return flight with the dive center. Avoid planning a morning dive followed by a flight immediately after lunch. The appropriate safe interval depends on the actual dive profile, the instructor's guidance and medical recommendations, not merely a general number in a travel guide.

Travelers planning to ascend into the [Andes near Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/) after the islands should also consider the gain in altitude by road. That, too, changes ambient pressure.

## Frequently asked questions about diving in Ecuador

### Where does Ada Tours' main diving itinerary in Ecuador take place?

In the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/), staying at Hotel Fiesta on [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/). Participants arrive via [Baltra](/ecuador/place/baltra-island/), and the dive center selects the sites.

### How many dives are included in the 4-day and 5-day options?

The 4-day option has 2 diving days and 4 dives; the 5-day option has 3 diving days and 6 dives. There is a break of approximately 1.5 hours between the day's two dives.

### Can I join without a PADI certificate?

The standard program requires PADI, NAUI, CMAS or an equivalent certification. Introductory dives and training are mentioned as separate possibilities. Their availability and terms must be agreed for the [specific diving tour](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-diving-4-5-days/).

### Is a dive at Gordon Rocks guaranteed?

No. [Gordon Rocks](/ecuador/place/gordon-rocks/) is among the possible dive sites, but access depends on weather, currents, the diver's experience and the operator's decisions. The site is known for demanding conditions.

### When can I fly after the final dive?

For repeated no-decompression dives, DAN's guideline is at least 18 hours before flying, with a longer interval needed in some circumstances. Coordinate your flight with the dive center before confirming the itinerary.

### What can I see in the Galápagos besides diving?

The itinerary includes [the Santa Cruz highlands and giant tortoises](/ecuador/santa-cruz-highlands/santa-cruz-highlands-tortoises-lunch/). If you want additional land-based excursions, compare [tours in Ecuador](/ecuador/tour/) and pay particular attention to transport connections involving the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/).

## Choosing a diving tour: start with the number of scuba days

Our catalog features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. These trips are very different from a standard beach vacation: on some, diving makes up most of the itinerary; on others, it is one of several active days. **Check the number of diving days first, then the number of dives scheduled on each day.** A longer tour around a country does not necessarily give you more time underwater.

| Itinerary | Diving component |
|---|---|
| [Galápagos, 4–5 days](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-diving-4-5-days/) | 2–3 days, 2 dives per day |
| [Costa Rica and Caño, 5 days](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-gems/) | One day near Caño Island |
| [Extreme Costa Rica, 13 days](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/) | One day near the Catalina Islands |

The table describes the underwater days included in the itineraries, not a guarantee that boats will depart in any weather. The Galápagos trip schedules either 4 or 6 dives, depending on its duration. The two Costa Rica itineraries specify a diving day, but there is no basis for automatically assuming that each includes 2 dives. The marine operator must confirm their number and conditions.

A journey built around diving also differs from a [wildlife-focused trip](/interests/wildlife/) or an [adventure vacation](/interests/adventure/), even though one route may combine several interests. Distinguish underwater activities from ordinary excursions: snorkeling with a mask, taking a boat ride and scuba diving have different requirements.

## The Galápagos: choose 4 or 5 days

[Galápagos Diving with Hotel Fiesta](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-diving-4-5-days/) is the most specialized of these itineraries. It begins on Baltra, with [Santa Cruz Island](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) serving as the base. The first day includes transfers, a visit to the [Santa Cruz highlands](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-highlands/) to see giant tortoises, an introduction to the dive center and an equipment check.

You can choose between:

- **4 days / 3 nights:** 2 diving days, with 2 dives each day, for a total of 4 scheduled dives.
- **5 days / 4 nights:** an additional third diving day, for a total of 6 scheduled dives.

The [independent Galápagos: Diving Day with 2 Dives excursion](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/galapagos-two-dive-day/) explains the format of an outing at sea. The group leaves the hotel in the morning, with a check dive, 2 dives, a surface interval with a snack, lunch and a return to the dive center. Travel time and the return schedule depend on the site's distance.

**The additional day really does add dives, rather than simply extra free time on the island.** If scuba diving is the main purpose of your trip, the 5-day option provides more opportunities. If you want to add the Galápagos to a longer journey while keeping the island stay relatively short, compare the 4-day option.

### Where exactly will the dives take place?

The excursion description lists possible locations around the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/), including [Bartolomé](/ecuador/place/bartolome-island/), [Floreana](/ecuador/place/floreana-island/), [Mosquera](/ecuador/place/mosquera-islet/) and [Gordon Rocks](/ecuador/place/gordon-rocks/). **These are potential dive sites, not an itinerary that visits every location listed.** The actual site depends on the day of the week, sea conditions, national park regulations and the group's diving experience.

Be particularly cautious about Gordon Rocks. It is known for currents and demanding conditions, and published descriptions express experience requirements in different ways. The dependable approach is to tell the dive center about your certification and diving history in advance and obtain confirmation that you can join the dives at the specific site selected. Even with suitable documents, the accompanying operator makes the final decision.

The Galápagos National Park administration defines authorized marine tourism sites and the activities permitted there. An attractive photograph of a location is no proof that a dive boat is allowed to conduct dives there on a particular day.

### What is included and what costs extra?

Both Galápagos options list accommodation at Fiesta, scheduled group transfers and excursions, specified meals, a basic diving-equipment package and an English-speaking divemaster. The equipment mentioned includes a wetsuit, regulator, buoyancy compensator, mask, fins, boots, weight system and cylinder.

Charged separately are return flights between mainland Ecuador and the Galápagos, national park entrance fees, the Transit Control Card, insurance, nitrox, a dive computer and certain accessories. Account for these costs when comparing the total travel budget. **The published accommodation-and-diving price is not the complete cost of reaching and visiting the islands.**

For regular diving, the program requires PADI, NAUI, CMAS or an equivalent certificate. Introductory sessions and training for uncertified participants are mentioned separately, but they are standalone options to be arranged with the center, not automatic admission to the main group. The stated minimum participant age is 12; additional medical requirements depend on health and diving history.

The [Ecuador diving tours collection](/interests/diving/tours/ecuador/) is useful for comparing this itinerary with other suitable trips in the country as they become available. For the destination's geography and ocean conditions, see our [guide to diving in Latin America](/interests/diving/). Here the focus is on the specific booking conditions and what the trip includes.

## Costa Rica: Caño Island on a 5-day itinerary

[Costa Rica: True Gems](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-gems/) combines [Corcovado National Park](/costa-rica/place/corcovado-national-park/) with [Caño Island](/costa-rica/place/cano-island/). This option suits travelers who want to experience the rainforest and spend one day scuba diving, rather than return to dive sites on several consecutive days.

According to the published itinerary, travelers fly from San José to Palmar Sur on day 2 and continue along the Sierpe River toward the Corcovado area. Day 3 features a nature excursion and a visit to the Sirena Station area. Diving near Caño is scheduled for day 4, followed by a return to the hotel; day 5 is reserved for the trip back to San José.

**The comparison with the Galápagos is straightforward:** Caño accounts for one underwater day, while much of the journey is devoted to the rainforest and wildlife encounters. The combination of these two environments is the reason to choose this itinerary. If you want to dive on several successive days, the 5-day Caño program does not replace the Galápagos option.

Caño lies within a protected Costa Rican marine area. The official conservation agency SINAC requires advance arrangements for access and regulates diving and snorkeling in designated zones. A diving day therefore cannot be considered unconditionally available simply because a tour starts on a given date: the site, operator, permit and sea conditions must all be coordinated.

The advertised tour price includes domestic San José–Palmar Sur–San José flights, transfers, entrance tickets, excursions with an English-speaking guide and meals according to the itinerary. However, its published description does not provide the same detailed breakdown of diving equipment and individual dives as the Galápagos itinerary. Have these details confirmed in the offer before paying.

## Costa Rica: Catalina on a 13-day adventure

[Extreme Costa Rica](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/) lasts 13 days and features a wide range of active experiences. Its route includes the Tortuguero canals, [rafting on the Pacuare River](/costa-rica/place/pacuare-river/), the Arenal area, the forests of Monteverde and the Pacific coast. Day 10 includes sport fishing near Flamingo; day 11 brings diving near the [Catalina Islands](/costa-rica/place/catalina-islands/).

The published description positions this diving day for **more experienced participants**. Strong currents and difficult surface conditions are possible. Sites of different depths are listed, but the actual dive profile and site availability depend on the operator, the sea and the diver's skills. This itinerary should not be promoted as a universally suitable first diving experience.

Catalina suits those who want varied adventure days in one country and already have scuba experience. For someone planning a holiday primarily around many diving days, it offers less underwater time than the dedicated Galápagos trip.

When comparing [Costa Rica diving tours](/interests/diving/tours/costa-rica/), bear in mind that Caño and Catalina are in different parts of the Pacific coast. The 5-day Caño trip focuses on the southwest and Corcovado; the 13-day Catalina option centers on a much larger overland adventure. They differ in route, intensity and participation requirements.

## Compare more than just the tour price

Before booking, request the same set of information for each option. That makes the comparison meaningful even when prices are calculated on different bases.

| What to check | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Diving days | Show how much time the trip actually allocates to diving |
| Number of dives | Clarifies the amount of diving you pay for |
| Certification and experience | Determine access to challenging dive sites |
| Equipment | Help avoid unexpected surcharges |
| Boat and transfers | Affect the length of the day |
| Flying after diving | Requires a safe interval |

For the Galápagos, the itinerary specifies 2 dives per day, basic equipment and the payment terms for additional gear. For Caño and Catalina, separately confirm the number of dives, required experience, equipment included in the price and who operates the outings. Do not apply one tour operator's or itinerary's terms to another trip.

Also consider anyone traveling with you who will not dive. The Galápagos product allows accompanying guests and snorkelers under separately stated payment conditions. Do not assume the Costa Rica itineraries offer identical arrangements without confirmation.

Prices on different tour pages may be per person sharing a double room, for a different trip duration or for a journey with more land-based activities. For a fair comparison, add necessary flights, permits, insurance and any extra equipment you choose to rent to the base price. Comparing only the first numbers on the tour pages will be misleading.

## Certification, medical requirements and the interval before flying

Independent scuba diving requires experience appropriate to the particular site. Tell the operator about your recent dives, current qualifications, health and need to hire equipment. Challenging sites may require evidence of previous dives or a skills assessment by an instructor.

**Allow enough time between the last dive and an airline flight.** Divers Alert Network recommends at least 12 hours after one no-decompression dive and 18 hours after several dives in one day or diving on multiple days. Dives involving mandatory decompression stops require a longer interval. These guidelines reduce the risk of decompression sickness but cannot eliminate it; a longer margin is preferable. Ascending to high altitude after diving also calls for caution.

The Galápagos itinerary includes a flight away from the islands after diving days, so coordinate the final boat outing and return flight in advance. The Caño itinerary likewise schedules a return flight the day after diving. The Catalina route includes an additional free day on the Pacific coast before the final flight day, but you must still calculate the real interval from the time diving ends.

Do not count on a specific encounter with a shark, manta ray or sea turtle. Even at well-known sites, wildlife remains wild and visibility and currents change. The local licensed operator decides when a boat can safely depart and which site to visit.

## Who should choose each option?

**Galápagos:** choose it if diving is the main activity, you have the required training and you want 4 or 6 scheduled dives on a relatively short trip. The deciding factor between 4 and 5 days is the additional day at sea, not merely the accommodation.

**Caño:** choose it if underwater wildlife and the Corcovado rainforest appeal to you equally. Leave space in your luggage for rainforest walks and confirm what is included in the single diving day in advance.

**Catalina:** this is a better fit for an experienced diver who wants a long adventure featuring rafting, volcanic landscapes and one day underwater. Diving is part of an activity-packed journey, rather than its central purpose.

If you mainly want to be near reefs, swim with a mask or relax by the sea, explore [beach tours](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/) and confirm individual water activities separately. Not every coastal itinerary is a scuba-diving product.

## Questions about choosing a diving tour

### How can I get more dives on a short trip?

Based on the confirmed itineraries, choose the [5-day Galápagos option](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-diving-4-5-days/), with 3 diving days and 2 dives per day. The 4-day option includes 2 days at sea. Both Costa Rica options in this collection have one diving day within a broader itinerary.

### Can I visit the Galápagos without a diving certificate?

Standard dives require certification from a recognized training organization. The itinerary separately mentions introductory experiences and training for uncertified guests, but these are different services and the dive center must confirm their availability. Challenging sites such as Gordon Rocks should not be assumed suitable for beginners.

### Are all flights and fees included in a diving tour?

There is no single rule across all products. On the Galápagos tour, the flight from the mainland, national park entrance fee and Transit Control Card are paid separately. The 5-day Costa Rica: True Gems itinerary lists San José–Palmar Sur–San José domestic flights among its inclusions. Read the specific product page.

### How does diving near Caño differ from diving near Catalina?

At [Caño Island](/costa-rica/place/cano-island/), diving forms part of a short trip that includes Corcovado. At the [Catalina Islands](/costa-rica/place/catalina-islands/), it is included in a longer adventure designed for experienced participants. Conditions concerning currents, boat travel and permits are established separately.

### Can I fly immediately after the final dive?

No. The minimum interval depends on the number and profile of your dives. Divers Alert Network guidelines specify 12 hours after one standard no-decompression dive and 18 hours after repeated dives or diving over several days. More time is preferable, and the final schedule should be agreed with the dive center before buying airline tickets.

## Excursions for events and festivals: Carnival in Rio de Janeiro

Our Events and Festivals section features experiences tied to actual events, rather than ordinary city sightseeing with a passing mention of a festival. The collection currently contains 2 independent excursions, both dedicated to Carnival in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/): [an evening at the Sambadrome with transfers](/brazil/rio-de-janeiro/carnival-sambadrome-transfer/) and [the 2027 Champions' Parade](/brazil/rio-de-janeiro/rio-champions-parade-2027-sambadrome/).

Dates and tickets matter particularly for Carnival. Even when the rest of a visitor's Rio itinerary is identical, attending a competition parade and watching the Champions' Parade are two different experiences. They take place on different days and require the corresponding tickets.

## How Carnival works at the Sambadrome

The Marquês de Sapucaí Sambadrome hosts Rio's main samba school parades. Large groups travel along the purpose-built parade avenue in elaborate costumes, accompanied by musicians, drum sections and moving scenic floats.

The competitive samba school performances follow a set timetable. After the results are announced, some of the schools return for the Champions' Parade. Travelers therefore choose between different stages of the same celebration.

Visiting the Sambadrome takes planning: roads around the event may close, traffic can be heavy, and performances continue late into the night. Your sector determines the view, the entrance you use and the arrangements for getting back after the show.

## Carnival with hotel transfers

The [Carnival at the Sambadrome with Hotel Transfers excursion](/brazil/rio-de-janeiro/carnival-sambadrome-transfer/) is an evening visit to a samba school parade. The itinerary includes transport from a Rio hotel to the Sambadrome and arrangements for the return journey.

Agree on the specific show date and sector separately when booking: the excursion description states that these depend on the reservation. Do not assume that one ticket grants entry to every Carnival evening or any sector.

This option suits visitors who are already staying in Rio and want to add a Carnival evening to their sightseeing plans. Allow time to recover the following day, since the celebrations end late.

## The 2027 Carnival Champions' Parade

In 2027, the Special Group samba schools' competitive performances are scheduled for **February 7, 8 and 9**, with the **Champions' Parade on Saturday, February 13, 2027**. These dates appear in the calendar published by the organizer, LIESA.

[Ada Tours' 2027 Champions' Parade excursion](/brazil/rio-de-janeiro/rio-champions-parade-2027-sambadrome/) includes an admission ticket and hotel–Sambadrome–hotel transfers. The description specifies a group visit, with the performance lasting through the evening and night.

Unlike the competition parades, this event brings the highest-scoring schools back onto the avenue for another performance. When planning a future visit, the final list of Champions' Parade participants cannot yet be treated as definitive: it is determined by the results of the Carnival competition.

The excursion is tied to this particular event in 2027. Conditions for another year should not be applied to it automatically.

## Choosing a day and sector at the Sambadrome

Before booking, decide what matters most: the atmosphere of the competition, seeing a particular samba school or watching the top schools at the Champions' Parade. For a regular parade evening, confirm the event calendar, your sector and the organized transfer times.

The seating sector affects your distance from the parade avenue and how you experience the show. Different ticket categories can offer good views, but their positions and entrances vary. Obtain a ticket for a specific date and category rather than relying on the general word "Carnival."

Plan the journey back carefully. A parade may finish in the early hours of the morning, when getting around the city is very different from daytime travel.

## Combining Carnival with sightseeing in Rio

Before the evening show, you can explore [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), its historic neighborhoods and famous viewpoints. Leave enough time in the day's schedule to rest, get ready for the Sambadrome and travel to the venue.

The [Events and Festivals](/interests/events-and-festivals/) section features journeys in which the event itself is a substantial part of the itinerary. To choose a complete multi-day trip through Brazil, compare the [country's tours](/brazil/tour/) and check the exact dates spent in Rio.

Not every Rio excursion is a Carnival experience. A museum visit, city tour or walk around the Sambadrome at another time does not replace admission to a samba school performance.

## Preparing for a Carnival evening

Bring whatever identification your ticket conditions require, comfortable shoes, only essential belongings and protection against possible rain. The organizers set the rules for bags, cameras, drinks and other items, and those rules may change.

Carnival takes place in Rio's hot, humid summer. Spending many hours at the venue in the evening and at night nevertheless calls for suitable clothing and enough water within the venue's rules.

Families traveling with children should consider the length of the performances and the trip back after midnight. The most spectacular part of the event may take place very late.

### When is Rio's Champions' Parade in 2027?

According to the LIESA timetable, it is on **Saturday, February 13, 2027**. The [Champions' Parade excursion](/brazil/rio-de-janeiro/rio-champions-parade-2027-sambadrome/) is tied to this event.

### What is the difference between the competitive parades and the Champions' Parade?

The competitive evenings determine which samba schools place highest. The Champions' Parade takes place after the results and brings the best performers back for another show.

### Are transfers included in the Carnival excursion?

The [2027 Champions' Parade excursion](/brazil/rio-de-janeiro/rio-champions-parade-2027-sambadrome/) lists both the ticket and return transfers. For the other option, [Carnival at the Sambadrome](/brazil/rio-de-janeiro/carnival-sambadrome-transfer/), the sector and date are arranged when booking.

### Does this collection include other festivals?

We only include excursions that have actually been published. At present, 2 Carnival programs in Rio are confirmed; other events should not be assumed available without their own dedicated excursion product.

  Carnival in Rio de Janeiro, New Year's Eve on Copacabana, the Day of the Dead in Mexico and the Candelaria festival in Peru offer entirely different experiences. ## Traveling for festivals and celebrations: where to start

**The first question is which specific event you want to attend and what you will do on its main day.** You can spend a week in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) during Carnival without ever seeing the samba schools perform at the Sambadrome. You can celebrate New Year's Eve in Brazil but stay in another city, far from the festivities on Copacabana. The destination and the month of travel alone are therefore not enough.

An event-focused tour differs from a regular sightseeing itinerary because of a **fixed date on the calendar**. The day of the parade, concert or celebration determines the order of the rest of the trip. After an overnight show, allow time to rest; before it, leave a buffer for flights and transfers. This is particularly noticeable during Carnival, when a surge in visitors changes the way the city operates.

We offer {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} connected with events and festivals. You can compare current options in the [festival and event tours catalog](/interests/events-and-festivals/tours/). Some itineraries devote an entire evening or several days to the celebration; on others, the event forms part of a journey through multiple regions or countries. In every case, examine the exact daily itinerary and the list of included services.

If the event is only an additional wish and the main reason for traveling is history, nature or the ocean, compare this section with [cultural journeys](/interests/culture-and-history/) and [beach vacations](/interests/beach-holidays/). This helps you preserve the experience that matters most to you.

## Which Latin American celebrations should you choose?

These events differ in the way visitors participate. A Carnival performance viewed from the stands, a New Year's Eve gathering of thousands on a beach and family remembrance traditions in [Mexico](/mexico/) call for very different behavior, clothing and daily arrangements.

| Event | Distinctive experience |
|---|---|
| Rio Carnival | Samba school parades |
| Champions' Parade | Performances by the best schools |
| New Year's Eve in Rio | A night on Copacabana |
| Mexico's Day of the Dead | Family remembrance rituals |
| Candelaria in Peru | Dance and religious processions |

We offer specific itineraries built around these events. For example, a [Champions' Parade trip with a stay in Angra dos Reis](/brazil/tour/tropical-champions-parade-rio-angra-2027/) combines Carnival with the ocean; a [New Year's journey through Brazil, Argentina and Chile](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-new-year-11-days-2027/) connects the holiday night with visits to three countries; and a [Day of the Dead tour in Mexico](/mexico/tour/mexico-day-of-the-dead/) focuses on local traditions in late October and early November.

Begin by choosing the kind of event you want. Those who hope to see a major staged performance need one type of trip. Those who want to explore streets, learn about rituals and meet local people need another.

## Rio Carnival: the Sambadrome, Champions' Parade or street processions?

Brazilian Carnival takes several forms, and they are not interchangeable. Street parades and events take place in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and other parts of [Brazil](/brazil/), but the most famous televised images are associated with the samba schools performing at the Sambadrome, a venue purpose-built for parades.

### Main samba school parades

Samba schools proceed along a broad parade avenue with musicians, dancers, themed costumes and moving scenic floats. Performances continue into the early hours. For spectators, not only the date but also **the seat in a specific [Sambadrome](/brazil/rio-de-janeiro/carnival-sambadrome-transfer/) sector** matters: watching from the stands differs from viewing the show from a private box.

Simply purchasing a tour described as "for Carnival" does not prove that a ticket for a particular night is included. Check the parade's name, sector, ticket category, starting time, how to reach the venue and the return transfer. These details are specified in individual Ada Tours itineraries and may differ.

For example, the [Flavors of Brazil: Carnival, Paraty and Ilha Grande tour](/brazil/tour/carnival-flavors-rio-paraty-ilha-grande/) combines an evening of samba school performances with a journey to the Green Coast. It illustrates how Carnival can become the opening of a longer trip rather than its only activity. Read the specific offer for ticket and transfer conditions.

### The Champions' Parade: a separate night

**The Champions' Parade takes place after the competitive performances**, when the highest-scoring samba schools return to the Sambadrome. It is a distinct event with its own date and tickets. It is not equivalent to any other Carnival evening and cannot be replaced by attending a street parade.

The current [10-day Tropical Champions' Parade 2027: Rio and Angra dos Reis itinerary](/brazil/tour/tropical-champions-parade-rio-angra-2027/) includes an evening at the Sambadrome, a Carnival ticket and hotel–Sambadrome–hotel transfers. After Rio, the route continues to the coast at [Angra dos Reis](/brazil/place/angra-dos-reis/). These are **confirmed inclusions for this particular tour**, not the standard package for every Carnival trip.

Another approach is the [Champions' Parade tour through Brazil, Argentina and Chile](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-champions-parade-10-days-2027/). The celebration becomes part of a journey including Iguazu Falls, [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) and [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). With more journeys between destinations, it is important to assess flight times after Carnival.

### Street Carnival and blocos

The street Carnival groups known as *blocos* form a world of their own in [Rio](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). Their processions may take place in different neighborhoods and on dates that do not coincide with your chosen Sambadrome night. City authorities confirm schedules and routes in advance, and transport arrangements may change.

If your priority is to stroll among the revelers, hear the drumming and experience the city's traditions, choose an itinerary with time for street events. If your dream is to see large floats and samba school performances, focus on tickets for the specific parade. The two experiences can be combined when the dates and logistics line up.

For a comparison of Brazilian trips specifically, see the [Brazil events and festivals tours collection](/interests/events-and-festivals/tours/brazil/). It includes routes of different lengths combining Carnival with nature, beaches and city excursions.

## New Year's Eve on Copacabana: the celebration and the journey afterward

In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), New Year's Eve traditionally brings huge crowds to Copacabana Beach. The festivities are known for concerts, music and fireworks. The exact show program and traffic arrangements are approved anew each season. Do not assume that last year's timetable, transport restrictions or entertainment lineup will apply next year.

**For a New Year's tour, the plan for the evening of December 31 and the return after midnight are especially important.** During major celebrations, roads may close, metro operations may change and access by car may be restricted. The hotel's location and the way back can therefore matter more than its distance from the beach on a map.

On the [11-day New Year's trip through Brazil, Argentina and Chile](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-new-year-11-days-2027/), celebrating on Copacabana is combined with a visit to Iguazu and a tango show in [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). The tour description lists a New Year's dinner and a hotel party as optional extras. They cannot be treated as automatically included simply because the itinerary contains a festive evening.

If you would rather celebrate closer to nature or away from large crowds, discuss alternative New Year's destinations and a suitable itinerary in advance. The [multi-country journeys catalog](/multi-country/) is useful if you want to add Argentina, Chile or other destinations to Rio, but visiting several countries does not itself guarantee a particular celebration.

### Planning the days around December 31

When possible, arrive before the main evening so that a delayed international flight does not jeopardize the only event of your trip. Avoid scheduling an early departure and a long transfer the morning after a late-night celebration. Distribute [Rio](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) sightseeing, including [Sugarloaf Mountain](/brazil/place/sugarloaf-mountain/) and [Corcovado](/brazil/place/corcovado-christ-the-redeemer/), across other days while taking attraction opening hours into account.

If you are planning a dinner, a special hotel event or entry to a restricted-capacity venue, confirm tickets, access requirements and prices separately. A free public celebration and a paid private party are different services.

## Mexico's Day of the Dead: remembrance, altars and living traditions

Mexico's Día de los Muertos takes place in late October and early November. Its meaning centers on remembering loved ones who have died. Families create altars with photographs, flowers and offerings, visit cemeteries and prepare special foods. UNESCO recognizes the tradition as intangible cultural heritage.

**It is about much more than colorful costumes or a large street performance.** Altar decorations and behavior during remembrance ceremonies vary among communities and regions. Visitors should respect family rituals, ask permission before photographing people and avoid interrupting ceremonies just to take pictures.

The [Day of the Dead in Mexico tour](/mexico/tour/mexico-day-of-the-dead/) is organized around the holiday dates. Over 9 days, it connects [Mexico City](/mexico/place/mexico-city-and-teotihuacan/), [Teotihuacan](/mexico/place/teotihuacan/), [Puebla](/mexico/place/puebla/), [Atlixco](/mexico/place/atlixco/), [Mixquic](/mexico/place/mixquic/) and [Xochimilco](/mexico/place/xochimilco/). The itinerary includes historical sightseeing and visits to places associated with family remembrance, with special emphasis on October 31, November 1 and November 2.

This journey suits those who want to understand traditions through real places and local practices. If you want to explore archaeology and colonial cities outside the festive period, look separately at [Mexico](/mexico/) and [cultural and historical tours](/interests/culture-and-history/). The festival trip depends on the calendar, whereas a regular cultural route offers more freedom to choose your travel month.

## The Candelaria festival in Peru: Puno, music and dance

Each February, the city of [Puno](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) on Lake Titicaca hosts the festival of the Virgin of Candelaria. It brings together Catholic religious observances, Andean traditions, processions, music, costumes and dance performances. UNESCO added the festival to the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2014.

Travelers should distinguish church ceremonies, processions and competitive dance performances: they use different venues, schedules and codes of conduct. The festivities last more than a day, so your arrival in [Puno](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) should match the particular event you hope to attend, rather than merely the general festival dates.

The published [13-day Peru: History of a Great Empire and the Festival of Saint Candelaria itinerary](/peru/tour/peru-inca-empire-candelaria-festival/) combines a visit to Puno and the festivities with [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), [Colca Canyon](/peru/place/colca-canyon/) and [Arequipa](/peru/place/arequipa/). It is an example of an event-centered journey that integrates participation in a local tradition into a broader cultural trip.

**[Puno](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) is high in the Andes.** Visitors arriving from low altitudes need to consider the pace of travel and time to acclimatize. Long processions and walking during festival days may add physical demands, so compare the itinerary and accommodation arrangements in advance. Other ways to explore the country can be found on the [Peru](/peru/) page.

## Building an itinerary around the main event

An event-focused journey has three parts: traveling to the celebration, the event itself and traveling afterward. Problems most often arise when the schedule is too tight between these stages.

**Before the event.** Do not schedule an international arrival immediately before your one paid parade. Allow for connections, travel to the hotel, possible delays and the need to collect a ticket or entrance instructions. If the ticket is valid for one particular night, lost time may be impossible to recover.

**On event day.** Leave time for rest, meals, getting to the venue and security checks. A crowded festival or overnight parade calls for a different pace from an ordinary city excursion. Avoid combining a long evening event with a packed sightseeing program starting early in the morning.

**After the event.** Plan a proper night's sleep and time for the onward journey. The days following a major festival are an excellent time to add relaxed days by the sea. For example, Rio can be combined with [Angra dos Reis](/brazil/place/angra-dos-reis/), as in the [Champions' Parade and beach holiday tour](/brazil/tour/tropical-champions-parade-rio-angra-2027/). If you prefer new cities to beaches, explore routes combining Carnival with neighboring countries, but assess the number of flights.

The straight-line distance between two places on a map does not tell you how long you will spend navigating road closures, checking in for a flight and reaching the airport. Complex routes are better planned by actual hours rather than day numbers alone.

## Tickets, transfers and participation: what to check

Words like "Carnival," "New Year" or "Festival" in a tour title do not yet tell you which services are included. Compare each offer point by point.

| What to check | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Type of event | Parade, festival or concert |
| Date and time | Each event has its own calendar |
| Ticket and sector | Determine how you watch the event |
| Return transfer | Transport may be limited at night |
| Hotel and location | Consider travel time and rest |
| Payment for extras | Dinner or a private box may cost extra |

Some Carnival itineraries do include Sambadrome admission and round-trip transfers. For example, these are explicitly listed in the [Champions' Parade tour with Angra dos Reis](/brazil/tour/tropical-champions-parade-rio-angra-2027/). Other offers require a separate review of ticket coverage, accompanying services and exact terms. On New Year's tours, the festive dinner may also be an extra.

Check the currency and price basis as well: per person, per group, in a double room or in a single room. Do not compare offers using one price figure without looking at the inclusions. If your main goal is one particular night and seating sector, confirm those details first, then choose the hotel and any additional excursions.

## An event plus beaches, history or gastronomy

After the main celebration, you can devote several days to another interest if the chosen itinerary actually includes it.

**Carnival + ocean.** Many travelers prefer to relax after overnight shows. The [Flavors of Brazil tour](/brazil/tour/carnival-flavors-rio-paraty-ilha-grande/) links Rio with [Paraty](/brazil/place/paraty/) and [Ilha Grande](/brazil/place/ilha-grande/), adding nature and beach stops to the Carnival program. If the sea is your main priority, compare it with [beach trips](/interests/beach-holidays/).

**Festival + history.** The Day of the Dead in [Mexico](/mexico/) and Candelaria in [Peru](/peru/) are closely tied to local traditions. After the celebration, you can naturally continue exploring historic neighborhoods, museums and monuments. On other dates, you can visit the same countries without having to plan around a festival.

**Carnival + several countries.** The [Champions' Parade, Iguazu, tango and wine itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-champions-parade-10-days-2027/) combines a spectacular Carnival night with independent experiences in [Argentina](/argentina/) and [Chile](/chile/). Check the time allocated to borders, flights and excursions so that the main event does not displace the other goals of the trip.

**Festival + local cuisine.** Festive dishes can be a memorable part of a culinary journey, but the inclusion of a holiday dinner does not by itself turn a trip into a [food and wine tour](/interests/food-and-wine/). If wineries, tastings or cooking activities matter to you, check the relevant days separately.

Do not add activities merely to make the list of cities longer. A well-designed combination leaves enough time both for the main celebration and for the second objective.

## When to book a festival trip and what to consider

Fixed-date events make it possible to decide on travel dates well in advance, but ticket, hotel and transport prices and availability depend on demand and the particular season. The essential starting point is a confirmed event calendar and a clear idea of how you want to participate.

**For Carnival,** check the official dates of the competitive parades, Champions' Parade and street processions separately. They may fall on different days. Consider the hotel and ticket for the required night together with transport to and from the Sambadrome.

**For New Year's Eve,** decide in advance whether you want to join the crowds on Copacabana, celebrate at a restaurant or stay at your hotel. City traffic restrictions and public transport arrangements are issued separately each season; last year's instructions cannot be relied on as a guaranteed timetable for the next celebration.

**For the Day of the Dead,** the dates fall in late October and early November, but remembrance ceremonies and public events vary by city and community. Do not expect the same experience everywhere in [Mexico](/mexico/).

**For Candelaria,** focus on the February calendar in [Puno](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) and confirm the dates of the processions and performances you want to attend. High altitude and long transfers between Andean cities add further considerations to the festival logistics.

Before purchasing, check whether the events and transfers are included in the actual quoted price. If a ticket or precise timetable has not been confirmed, clarify the conditions before paying rather than assuming they will automatically be arranged.

## Frequently asked questions about festival and event travel

### Is visiting Rio during Carnival enough to see a samba school parade?

No. The parade at the [Sambadrome](/brazil/rio-de-janeiro/carnival-sambadrome-transfer/) takes place on specific nights and has separate admission requirements. Street Carnival and the samba school performances are different events. If the parade is your main reason for traveling, choose a tour that specifies the parade, ticket and transfer arrangements.

### How does the Champions' Parade differ from the main Carnival parades?

During the main parades, the samba schools compete. After the results are announced, the best schools perform again at the Champions' Parade. These events have different dates and tickets. Check the event name, not just the word "Carnival," when booking.

### Do I need to buy a ticket for New Year's Eve on Copacabana?

Public celebrations on the beach and paid events at hotels or restaurants operate differently. Check the official arrangements for public access and additional private services for the specific year. If a tour mentions a New Year's dinner, find out separately whether that dinner is included.

### Is Mexico's Day of the Dead a Carnival?

No. The celebration honors deceased relatives, with rituals involving altars, flowers, offerings and visits to cemeteries. Some places host public processions and performances, but family ceremonies deserve respectful treatment. To discover these traditions, consider the [dedicated Mexico itinerary](/mexico/tour/mexico-day-of-the-dead/).

### In which months does the Candelaria festival take place in [Puno](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/)?

The festivities take place in February. They combine religious processions and dance performances, with schedules that may vary. Match the specific days you want to attend to your route and account for Puno's high altitude.

### Can I combine Carnival with a beach holiday?

Yes, provided the chosen itinerary sets aside separate days by the sea. For example, the [Rio, Paraty and Ilha Grande tour](/brazil/tour/carnival-flavors-rio-paraty-ilha-grande/) combines Carnival events with the Green Coast. Compare the number of nights by the ocean, travel after the celebrations and available free time.

### Are event-focused tours suitable for families with children?

That depends on the children's ages, event duration and schedule. Late-night performances at the Sambadrome and extremely crowded celebrations can be more demanding than daytime cultural festivals. Choose a suitable family experience based on the specific itinerary; our [family tours section](/interests/family-tours/) offers other options to compare.

### What if the date of the main event changes?

Check the organizer's current calendar and the tour operator's conditions before confirming tickets, hotels and flights. A change to the event schedule may affect the entire itinerary. A time buffer and a clear understanding of which trip components depend on the specific date are therefore valuable.
